sentences.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，諱榮，太祖之養子，蓋聖穆皇后之侄也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong the Sagely Martial and Filial, taboo name Rong, was the adopted son of Emperor Taizu and was the nephew of Empress Shengmu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, posthumously titled Sagely Martial and Filial, bore the personal name Rong. He was Emperor Taizu's adopted son and a nephew of Empress Shengmu.

sentences.zh: 本姓柴氏，父守禮，太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: His original surname was the Chai clan; his father was Shouli, who had retired as Grand Master of Remonstrance for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was born into the Chai clan. His father Shouli had retired from office as Grand Master of Remonstrance for the Heir Apparent.

translations.literal: (Editorial note:
translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：柴翁者，嘗獨居室，人以為司冥事。

translations.literal: (From the 《Longping ji》: The old man Chai once lived alone in his chamber; people thought he attended to infernal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Longping ji》: An old man of the Chai clan once lived alone in his chamber, and people believed he had dealings with the realm of the dead.

sentences.zh: 一日，笑不止，妻問其故，不答。

translations.literal: One day he laughed without stopping; his wife asked the reason, but he would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: One day he laughed without cease. When his wife asked why, he would not tell her.

sentences.zh: 翁嗜飲，妻醉之以酒，乃曰：「上帝有命，郭郎為天子。

translations.literal: The old man loved drink; his wife made him drunk with wine, whereupon he said: "Heaven has commanded that Lord Guo shall become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The old man loved wine. His wife plied him with drink until he was drunk, and then he said, "Heaven has decreed that Lord Guo shall become emperor."

sentences.zh: 」考柴翁即守禮之父，史佚其名。）〉

translations.literal: " Investigation shows that the old man Chai was the father of Shouli; the history omits his personal name.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " It is established that this old man Chai was Shouli's father, though the history does not record his personal name.)]

sentences.zh: 帝以唐天祐十八年，歲在辛巳，九月二十四日丙午，生於邢州之別墅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, day bingwu, in the eighteenth year of Tang Tianyou, year xinsi, at a villa in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of 921, the eighteenth year of Tang Tianyou, cyclical year xinsi, at a country estate in Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年未童冠，因侍聖穆皇后，在太祖左右。

translations.literal: Before he had reached the age of the cap, he attended Empress Shengmu and was at Emperor Taizu's side.
translations.idiomatic: While still a boy, he attended Empress Shengmu and remained close at Emperor Taizu's side.

sentences.zh: 時太祖無子，家道淪落，然以帝謹厚，故以庶事委之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizu had no sons and the family fortunes had declined, but because the Emperor was prudent and sincere, miscellaneous affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then had no sons of his own, and the family's fortunes had fallen on hard times. Because Rong was prudent and steadfast, Taizu entrusted him with the household's day-to-day affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝悉心經度，資用獲濟，太祖甚憐之，乃養為己子。

translations.literal: The Emperor managed affairs with full care; supplies and expenses were provided for, and Emperor Taizu cherished him greatly, whereupon he was adopted as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: He managed everything with scrupulous care and kept the household supplied. Taizu grew deeply fond of him and adopted him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 漢初，太祖以佐命功為樞密副使，帝始授左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Emperor Taizu was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs for his merit in assisting the mandate; the Emperor was first appointed Left Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han was founded, Taizu was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs for his service in establishing the dynasty. Rong received his first appointment as Left Gate Guard General.

translations.literal: (Editorial note:
translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《國老談苑》云：周世宗在漢為諸衛將軍，嘗遊畿甸，謁縣令，忘其姓名，令方聚邑客蒱博，勿得見，世宗頗銜之。

translations.literal: (The 《Guolao tanyuan》 states: When Zhou Shizong was a guard general under Han, he once traveled in the capital region and called on a county magistrate, whose name is forgotten; the magistrate was just gathering local guests for gambling and would not receive him, and Shizong harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Guolao tanyuan》 records that while Shizong was still a guard general under the Later Han, he once traveled in the capital region and called on a county magistrate, whose name is not recorded. The magistrate was hosting local guests at dice and refused to see him, and Shizong took the slight hard.

sentences.zh: 及即位，令因部夫犯贓數百匹，宰相範質以具獄上奏，世宗曰：「親民之官，贓狀狼籍，法當處死。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, that magistrate, through corvée laborers, committed embezzlement of several hundred bolts of silk; the Chief Minister Fan Zhi submitted the completed case for imperial decision, and Shizong said: "An official close to the people whose corruption is so flagrant should be put to death by law."
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, that same magistrate was found to have embezzled several hundred bolts of silk through corvée laborers. Chief Minister Fan Zhi submitted the completed case for decision. Shizong said, "An official charged with caring for the people whose corruption is this blatant deserves death under the law."

sentences.zh: 」質奏曰：「受所監臨財物有罪，上贓雖多，法不至死。

translations.literal: " Fan Zhi memorialized: "Receiving property from those under one's supervision is an offense; though the amount embezzled is large, the law does not reach to death."
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhi replied, "Taking property from those under one's supervision is indeed a crime, but even when the amount is large, the statute does not prescribe death."

sentences.zh: 」世宗怒，厲聲曰：「法者自古帝王之所制，本以防奸，朕立法殺贓吏，非酷刑也。

translations.literal: " Shizong grew angry and said in a stern voice: "Law has been made by emperors and kings since antiquity, fundamentally to guard against wickedness; I make law to execute corrupt officials—this is not cruel punishment."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong grew angry and said sharply, "Law has been made by rulers since antiquity precisely to guard against wickedness. When I legislate the execution of corrupt officials, that is not cruel punishment."

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「陛下殺之則可，若付有司，臣不敢署敕。

translations.literal: " Fan Zhi said: "Your Majesty may execute him if you wish; but if the case is handed to the judicial offices, this subject dares not sign the edict."
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Zhi said, "Your Majesty may execute him if you wish, but if the case is handed to the judicial offices, I will not sign the edict."

sentences.zh: 」遂貸其命。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon his life was spared.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " In the end his life was spared.)]

sentences.zh: 二年，太祖鎮鄴，改天雄軍牙內都指揮使，領貴州刺史、檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Emperor Taizu was stationed at Ye, he was changed to Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Guards of the Tianxiong Army, and concurrently held the posts of Prefect of Gui Prefecture and Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Taizu took command at Ye, Rong was made Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Guards of the Tianxiong Army and concurrently served as Prefect of Gui Prefecture and Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，留帝守鄴城。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year, Emperor Taizu entered the capital to quell internal turmoil and left the Emperor to guard Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Taizu marched to the capital to quell internal strife and left Rong to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年正月，太祖踐祚，帝懇求入覲，忽夢至河而不得渡，尋授澶州節度使、檢校太保，封太原郡侯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Guangshun, Emperor Taizu ascended the throne; the Emperor earnestly requested an audience, suddenly dreamed of reaching a river but being unable to cross, and soon thereafter was appointed Military Commissioner of Cao Prefecture, Acting Grand Guardian, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Guangshun 1, year 951, Taizu took the throne. Rong urgently petitioned for an audience, then dreamed that he came to a river but could not cross. Soon after he was appointed Military Commissioner of Cao Prefecture and Acting Grand Guardian, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝在鎮，為政清肅，盜不犯境。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was in his command, his governance was clear and austere, and bandits did not violate the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In his commandery his rule was clear and strict, and bandits did not trouble his territory.

sentences.zh: 先是，澶之裏巷湫隘，公署毀圯，帝即廣其街肆，增其廨宇，吏民賴之。

translations.literal: Previously the lanes of Cao were cramped and low, and the government offices were ruined and collapsed; the Emperor then broadened its market streets and enlarged its official buildings, and officials and people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao's lanes had been cramped and its government offices dilapidated. He widened the market streets, rebuilt the official quarters, and officials and commoners alike benefited.

translations.literal: (Editorial note:
translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王贊傳》：周世宗鎮澶淵，每旬決囚，贊引律令，辨析中理。

translations.literal: (From the 《Song shi》, biography of Wang Zan: When Zhou Shizong was stationed at Cao, he judged prisoners every ten days; Zan cited statutes and ordinances and analyzed cases with sound reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Song shi》, biography of Wang Zan: When Shizong held Cao, he heard criminal cases every ten days. Wang Zan cited statutes and analyzed each case with sound reasoning.

sentences.zh: 問之，知其嘗事學問，即署右職。）〉

translations.literal: On inquiry, it was learned that he had once pursued learning, whereupon he was appointed to a senior post.)〉
translations.idiomatic: On inquiry Shizong learned that he had pursued scholarship, and at once gave him a senior appointment.)]

sentences.zh: 二年正月，兗州慕容彥超反，帝累表請征行，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Murong Yanchao of Yan Prefecture rebelled; the Emperor repeatedly memorialized requesting to go on campaign, and Emperor Taizu commended this.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Murong Yanchao of Yan Prefecture rebelled. Rong repeatedly petitioned to lead the campaign, and Taizu praised his zeal.

sentences.zh: 及曹英等東討，數月無功，太祖欲親征，召群臣議其事，宰臣馮道奏以方當盛夏，車駕不宜沖冒。

translations.literal: When Cao Ying and others campaigned eastward for several months without success, Emperor Taizu wished to campaign in person, summoned the ministers to discuss the matter, and the Chief Minister Feng Dao memorialized that it was just the height of summer and the imperial carriage should not brave the heat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Ying and others had campaigned in the east for months without success, Taizu wished to take the field himself. He summoned the ministers to discuss the matter. Chief Minister Feng Dao argued that it was high summer and the imperial carriage should not brave the heat.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「寇不可玩。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu said: "Bandits must not be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Rebels must not be trifled with."

sentences.zh: 如朕不可行，當使澶州兒子擊賊，方辦吾事。

translations.literal: If I cannot go, then the son at Cao Prefecture should strike the bandits—that will settle my affair."
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot go myself, then let my boy at Cao strike the rebels. That will settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 」時樞密王峻意不欲帝將兵，故太祖親征。

translations.literal: At that time the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jun did not wish the Emperor to command troops, and therefore Emperor Taizu campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, did not want Rong to command troops, so Taizu took the field himself.

sentences.zh: 六月，兗州平。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yan Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yan Prefecture was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he was further appointed Acting Grand Tutor and Associate Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was further appointed Acting Grand Tutor and Associate Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝入覲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, the Emperor came to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he came to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 三月，授開封尹兼功德使，封晉王。

translations.literal: In the third month, he was appointed Prefect of Kaifeng and concurrently Commissioner of Meritorious Deeds, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Prefect of Kaifeng and Commissioner of Meritorious Deeds, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 二月庚戌，潞州奏，河東劉崇與契丹大將軍楊袞，舉兵南指。

translations.literal: On day gengxu of the second month, Lu Prefecture reported that Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Grand General Yang Gun had raised troops and were pointing south.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the second month Lu Prefecture reported that Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Grand General Yang Gun had raised troops and were marching south.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，宰臣馮道率百僚上表請御殿，凡三上，允之。

translations.literal: On day renxu, the Chief Minister Feng Dao led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial requesting that he hold court; they submitted three times, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day Chief Minister Feng Dao led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial asking him to hold court. They submitted three times before he assented.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以中書令馮道充山陵使，太常卿田敏充禮儀使，兵部尚書張昭充鹵簿使，御史中丞張煦充儀仗使，開封少尹、權判府事王敏充橋道使。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Zhongshu Ling Feng Dao was made Commissioner for the Imperial Tomb, Minister of Rites Tian Min Commissioner for Ritual, Minister of War Zhang Zhao Commissioner for the Imperial Train, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xu Commissioner for Ceremonial Arms, and Junior Prefect of Kaifeng and Acting Administrator Wang Min Commissioner for Bridges and Roads.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Feng Dao was made Commissioner for the Imperial Tomb, Tian Min Commissioner for Ritual, Zhang Zhao Commissioner for the Imperial Train, Zhang Xu Commissioner for Ceremonial Arms, and Wang Min, Junior Prefect of Kaifeng and acting administrator, Commissioner for Bridges and Roads.

sentences.zh: 河東賊將張暉率前鋒自團柏谷入寇，帝召群臣議親征。

translations.literal: The Hedong rebel general Zhang Hui led the vanguard in invading through Tuanbai Valley; the Emperor summoned the ministers to discuss campaigning in person.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong rebel general Zhang Hui led the vanguard through Tuanbai Valley. The emperor summoned the ministers to discuss a personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 宰臣馮道等奏，以劉崇自平陽奔遁之後，勢弱氣奪，未有復振之理，竊慮聲言自來，以誤於我，陛下纂嗣之初，先帝山陵有日，人心易搖，不宜輕舉，命將禦寇，深以為便。

translations.literal: The Chief Minister Feng Dao and others memorialized that since Liu Chong fled in panic from Pingyang, his strength was weak and his spirit broken, and there was no reason he could recover; they privately feared that reports had come of their own accord to mislead us; at the beginning of Your Majesty's succession, the former emperor's tomb rites were imminent, hearts were easily shaken, and one should not act lightly—ordering generals to repel the enemy would be deeply advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Feng Dao and others argued that since Liu Chong had fled Pingyang in panic, his forces were spent and demoralized and could not recover. They feared the reports might be misleading. With Your Majesty newly enthroned and the former emperor's funeral imminent, morale was fragile and a rash move was unwise; sending generals to repel the enemy would be far safer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「劉崇幸我大喪，聞我新立，自謂良便，必發狂謀，謂天下可取，謂神器可圖，此際必來，斷無疑耳！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Liu Chong, taking advantage of our great mourning and hearing that I am newly enthroned, will think the moment favorable, surely hatch reckless schemes, think the realm can be taken and the sacred vessel seized—at this juncture he is certain to come; there is absolutely no doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Liu Chong will seize on our mourning and on my recent accession. He will think the moment perfect, hatch reckless schemes, and imagine he can seize the realm and the throne. He is certain to come now—there is no doubt of it!"

sentences.zh: 」馮道等以帝銳於親征，因固諍之。

translations.literal: " Feng Dao and others, seeing the Emperor keen on campaigning in person, therefore remonstrated firmly.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao and the others, seeing how determined he was to take the field, remonstrated all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔唐太宗之創業，靡不親征，朕何憚焉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When Emperor Taizong of Tang founded his enterprise, there was nothing he did not campaign for in person—what should I fear!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Emperor Taizong of Tang built his empire, he campaigned in person at every turn. What have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下未可便學太宗。

translations.literal: " Dao said: "Your Majesty cannot yet simply imitate Taizong."
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao said, "Your Majesty cannot yet simply take Taizong as your model."

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「劉崇烏合之眾，茍遇王師，必如山壓卵耳。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also said: "Liu Chong's rabble, if they meet the royal army, will surely be like a mountain crushing an egg."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor added, "Liu Chong's rabble, if they meet the imperial army, will be crushed like a mountain falling on an egg."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「不知陛下作得山否？

translations.literal: " Dao said: "I do not know whether Your Majesty can be that mountain?"
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao replied, "I wonder whether Your Majesty can be that mountain?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased and ended the discussion.

sentences.zh: 詔諸道募山林亡命之徒有勇力者送於闕下，仍目之為強人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the various circuits to recruit from the mountains and forests fugitives and outlaws with strength and courage and send them to the court, still designating them as "strong men."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered every circuit to recruit fugitives and outlaws from the hills who had strength and courage and send them to court. They were called "strong men."

sentences.zh: 帝以趫捷勇猛之士多出於群盜中，故令所在招納，有應命者，即貸其罪，以禁衛處之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that swift and fierce warriors mostly came from among bandit gangs, therefore ordered localities to recruit them; those who answered the call had their crimes pardoned and were placed in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that the swiftest and fiercest fighters often came from outlaw bands, so he ordered recruitment everywhere. Those who answered had their crimes pardoned and were placed in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 至有朝行殺奪，暮升軍籍，讎人遇之不敢仰視。

translations.literal: There were even cases of robbery and murder in the morning and enrollment in the army rolls by evening; enemies who met them did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Some robbed and killed in the morning and were enrolled in the army by evening. Their enemies did not dare meet their eyes.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦患之，其後頗有不獲宥者。

translations.literal: The Emperor in his mind was also troubled by this; afterward many were not granted pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself grew troubled by this, and afterward many were not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，潞州奏，河東劉崇入寇，兵馬監押穆令均部下兵士為賊軍所襲，官軍不利。

translations.literal: On day dingchou of the third month, Lu Prefecture reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded; the troops under Military Supervisor Mu Lingjun were attacked by the rebel army, and the government forces fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the third month Lu Prefecture reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded. Troops under Military Supervisor Mu Lingjun were ambushed and the government forces suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 詔天雄軍節度使符彥卿領兵自磁州固鎮路赴潞州，以澶州節度使郭崇副之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army Fu Yanqing to lead troops from Cizhou by the Guzhen route toward Lu Prefecture, with Military Commissioner of Cao Prefecture Guo Chong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing, Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army, was ordered to lead troops from Cizhou along the Guzhen route toward Lu, with Guo Chong of Cao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔河中節度使王彥超領兵取晉州路東向邀擊，以陜府節度使韓通為副。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Military Commissioner of Hezhong Wang Yanchao to lead troops by the Jin Prefecture route eastward to intercept, with Military Commissioner of Shaanfu Han Tong as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was ordered to advance along the Jin Prefecture route and intercept from the east, with Han Tong of Shaanfu as deputy.

sentences.zh: 命宣徽使向訓、馬軍都指揮使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使何徽、滑州節度使白重贊、鄭州防禦使史彥超、前耀州團練使符彥能等，領兵先赴澤州。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun, Cavalry Commander-in-Chief Fan Aineng, Infantry Commander-in-Chief He Hui, Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Bai Chongzan, Defense Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture Shi Yanchao, former Regimental Commander of Yao Prefecture Fu Yanneng, and others were ordered to lead troops first to Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, Fan Aineng, He Hui, Bai Chongzan, Shi Yanchao, Fu Yanneng, and others were ordered to advance first to Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，制：「大赦天下，常赦所不原者，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, an ordinance stated: "A great amnesty is proclaimed for the realm; those not normally pardoned in regular amnesties are all pardoned and absolved."
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day an ordinance proclaimed a great amnesty for the realm, pardoning even offenses normally excluded from routine amnesties.

sentences.zh: 諸貶降責授官，量與升陟敘用，應配流徒役人，並放逐便。

translations.literal: All demoted, degraded, and reassigned officials are to be promoted and reemployed as appropriate; all those sentenced to exile, penal servitude, or corvée are to be released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted and reassigned officials were to be promoted and reemployed as appropriate. All those in exile, penal servitude, or corvée were to be released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 諸道州府所欠去年夏秋租稅並放。

translations.literal: All unpaid summer and autumn rent and tax from last year owed by the various circuits, prefectures, and districts are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Unpaid summer and autumn rent and tax from the previous year owed by every circuit, prefecture, and district were remitted.

sentences.zh: 內外見任、前文武職官並與加恩，父母在者並與恩澤，亡沒者與封贈，其母妻未敘者，特與敘封」云。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials currently serving inside and outside the court and all former officials receive added favor; those whose parents are living receive favor as well; the deceased receive posthumous titles and gifts; mothers and wives not yet ennobled receive special enfeoffment," it stated.
translations.idiomatic: All serving and former civil and military officials received added favors. Living parents received grants of favor; the deceased received posthumous titles; mothers and wives not yet ennobled received special enfeoffment," the ordinance stated.

sentences.zh: 前涇州節度使史匡懿卒。

translations.literal: The former Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture Shi Kuangyi died.
translations.idiomatic: The former Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture, Shi Kuangyi, died.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以劉崇入寇，車駕取今月十一日親征。

translations.literal: On day guiwei, an edict stated that because Liu Chong had invaded, the imperial carriage would campaign in person on the eleventh day of this month.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day an edict announced that because Liu Chong had invaded, the emperor would take the field in person on the eleventh of the month.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以樞密使鄭仁誨為東京留守。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zheng Renhui was made Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day Zheng Renhui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，車駕發京師。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, the imperial carriage departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day the emperor departed the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，至澤州。

translations.literal: On day renchen, he reached Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day he reached Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，王師與河東劉崇、契丹楊袞大戰於高平，賊軍敗績。

translations.literal: On day guisi, the royal army fought a great battle with Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Yang Gun at Gaoping; the rebel army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day the imperial army fought Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitan Yang Gun in a great battle at Gaoping. The rebel army was routed.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕行次河陽，聞劉崇自潞而南，即倍程而進。

translations.literal: Initially, when the imperial carriage halted at Heyang and heard that Liu Chong was coming south from Lu, he immediately doubled his pace and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Heyang and heard that Liu Chong was marching south from Lu, he immediately pressed forward at double speed.

sentences.zh: 是月十八日至澤州，既晡，帝御戎服，觀兵於東北郊，距州十五里，夜宿於村舍。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of that month he reached Ze Prefecture; after the hour of shen, the Emperor donned military dress and reviewed the troops in the northeastern suburbs, fifteen li from the prefectural seat, and lodged that night in a village house.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Ze on the eighteenth. In late afternoon he put on military dress and reviewed the troops fifteen li northeast of the city, then spent the night in a farmhouse.

sentences.zh: 十九日，先鋒與賊軍相遇，賊陣於高平縣南之高原。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the vanguard met the rebel army; the rebels formed battle lines on the high plateau south of Gaoping County.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth the vanguard met the rebels, who drew up on the high ground south of Gaoping County.

sentences.zh: 有賊中來者，云：「劉崇自將騎三萬，並契丹萬餘騎，嚴陣以待官軍。

translations.literal: Someone came from among the rebels and said: "Liu Chong personally commands thirty thousand cavalry, together with more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen, drawn up in strict formation awaiting the government army."
translations.idiomatic: A man came from the rebel camp and reported, "Liu Chong commands thirty thousand cavalry in person, with more than ten thousand Khitan horsemen besides, all drawn up in tight formation awaiting the imperial army."

sentences.zh: 」帝促兵以擊之，崇東西列陣，頗亦嚴整。

translations.literal: " The Emperor urged the troops to attack; Chong deployed his lines east and west, also quite strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pressed the attack. Liu Chong deployed his forces in east-west lines, likewise in tight order.

sentences.zh: 乃令侍衛馬步軍都虞候李重進、滑州節度使白重贊將左，居陣之西廂；

translations.literal: He then ordered Chief Commandant of the Palace Cavalry and Infantry Li Chongjin and Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Bai Chongzan to command the left wing, stationed in the western flank of the formation;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chief Commandant Li Chongjin and Bai Chongzan of Hua to command the left wing on the western flank;

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使樊愛能、步軍都指揮使何徽將右，居陣之東廂；

translations.literal: Cavalry Commander-in-Chief Fan Aineng and Infantry Commander-in-Chief He Hui to command the right wing, stationed in the eastern flank of the formation;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Aineng and He Hui to command the right wing on the eastern flank;

sentences.zh: 宣徽使向訓、鄭州防禦使史彥超，以精騎當其中；

translations.literal: Commissioner Xiang Xun and Defense Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture Shi Yanchao to take elite cavalry in the center;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun and Shi Yanchao of Zheng to hold elite cavalry in the center;

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使張永德以禁兵衛蹕。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Zhang Yongde to guard the imperial procession with palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde to guard the imperial procession with palace troops.

sentences.zh: 帝介馬觀戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor, armored and mounted, observed the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched from horseback in armor.

sentences.zh: 兩軍交鋒，未幾，樊愛能、何徽望賊而遁，東廂騎軍亂，步軍解甲投賊，帝乃自率親騎，臨陣督戰。

translations.literal: When the two armies clashed, before long Fan Aineng and He Hui fled at sight of the rebels; the eastern wing cavalry fell into disorder, and the infantry cast off armor and surrendered to the enemy; the Emperor then personally led his elite cavalry to the front to direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after the armies clashed, Fan Aineng and He Hui fled at sight of the enemy. The eastern cavalry collapsed and the infantry threw down their armor and surrendered. The emperor then led his personal guard to the front to direct the fighting himself.

translations.literal: (Editorial note:
translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·馬仁瑀傳》：從世宗親征劉崇，王師不利，仁瑀謂眾曰：「主辱臣死！

translations.literal: (From the 《Longping ji》, biography of Ma Renyu: Following Shizong on the campaign against Liu Chong, when the royal army fared poorly, Renyu said to the troops: "When the lord is shamed, the minister must die!"
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Longping ji》, biography of Ma Renyu: On Shizong's campaign against Liu Chong, when the imperial army faltered, Renyu cried to the troops, "When the lord is shamed, the minister must die!"

sentences.zh: 」因躍馬大呼，引弓連斃將卒數十，士氣始振。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he leaped on his horse and shouted loudly, drew his bow and in succession killed several tens of officers and soldiers, and the troops' morale began to revive.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He spurred his horse forward, shouting, and with his bow killed dozens of enemy officers and men in succession until the army's spirit revived.)]

sentences.zh: 今上馳騎於陣前，先犯其鋒，戰士皆奮命爭先，賊軍大敗。

translations.literal: The present sovereign galloped before the battle lines and first struck their vanguard; the warriors all strove with their lives to take the lead, and the rebel army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The present sovereign charged to the front and struck the enemy vanguard first. Every soldier fought to outdo the rest, and the rebel army was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 日暮，賊萬餘人阻澗而陣，會劉詞領兵至，與大軍迫之，賊軍又潰，臨陣斬賊大將張暉及偽樞密使王延嗣。

translations.literal: At dusk, more than ten thousand rebels blocked a stream and formed lines; when Liu Ci arrived leading troops and joined the main army in pressing them, the rebel army collapsed again; on the field the rebel Grand General Zhang Hui and the false Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Yansi were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk more than ten thousand rebels held a stream and made a stand. Liu Ci arrived with reinforcements and, with the main army, pressed them until they broke again. The rebel generals Zhang Hui and the false Commissioner Wang Yansi were beheaded on the field.

sentences.zh: 諸將分兵追襲，僵屍棄甲填滿山谷。

translations.literal: The generals divided their forces in pursuit; corpses and cast-off armor filled the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The generals split their forces in pursuit. Corpses and discarded armor filled the valleys.

sentences.zh: 初夜，官軍至高平，降賊軍數千人，所獲輜重、兵器、駝馬、偽乘輿器服等不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In the first watch of the night the government army reached Gaoping; several thousand rebel troops surrendered; baggage trains, weapons, camels and horses, false imperial carriage regalia and robes captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first watch the army reached Gaoping. Several thousand rebels surrendered. Baggage, weapons, camels, horses, and counterfeit imperial regalia were captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 其夕，殺降軍二千餘人，我軍之降敵者亦皆就戮。

translations.literal: That evening, more than two thousand surrendered troops were killed; enemy soldiers who had surrendered to our army were also all executed.
translations.idiomatic: That evening more than two thousand surrendered rebels were put to death, and enemy soldiers who had surrendered to the imperial side were also executed.

sentences.zh: 初，兩軍之未整也，風自東北起，不便於我，及與賊軍相遇，風勢陡回，人情相悅。

translations.literal: Initially, before the two armies were fully arrayed, wind rose from the northeast, unfavorable to us; when we met the rebel army, the wind suddenly reversed, and men's hearts were mutually pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies were fully drawn up, a wind rose from the northeast to our disadvantage. When the enemy was met, the wind suddenly shifted, and morale lifted throughout the ranks.

sentences.zh: 戰之前夕，有大星如日，流行數丈，墜於賊營之上。

translations.literal: On the eve of battle, a great star bright as the sun streaked several zhang and fell upon the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle a great star bright as the sun streaked across the sky and fell on the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 及戰，北人望見官軍之上，有雲氣如龍虎之狀，則天之助順，亶其然乎！

translations.literal: During the battle, northerners saw above the government army cloud vapors shaped like dragons and tigers—truly Heaven aids the righteous; is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: During the fight northerners saw cloud shapes like dragons and tigers above the imperial army. Heaven truly favors the righteous cause—was there ever any doubt!

sentences.zh: 是日，危急之勢頃刻莫保，賴帝英武果敢，親臨寇敵，不然則社稷幾若綴旒矣。

translations.literal: That day, the perilous situation could not be preserved for a moment; it depended on the Emperor's martial valor and resolution in personally facing the enemy—otherwise the altars of state would nearly have hung by a single thread.
translations.idiomatic: That day disaster hung by a thread. Only the emperor's martial courage in facing the enemy in person saved the dynasty from hanging by a thread.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝宿於野次。

translations.literal: That evening, the Emperor lodged in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor camped in the open field.

sentences.zh: 甲午，次高平縣。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, he halted at Gaoping County.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day he halted at Gaoping County.

sentences.zh: 詔賜河東降軍二千餘人各絹二匹，並給其衣裝，鄉兵各給絹一匹，放還本部。

translations.literal: An edict granted each of the more than two thousand surrendered Hedong troops two bolts of silk and also provided their clothing; local militia each received one bolt of silk and were released to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted each of the more than two thousand surrendered Hedong troops two bolts of silk and restored their clothing. Local militiamen each received one bolt and were sent home.

sentences.zh: 是日大雨。

translations.literal: That day there was heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕至潞州。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, the imperial carriage reached Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day the emperor reached Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河南府上言，前青州節度使常思卒。

translations.literal: Henan Prefecture reported that the former Military Commissioner of Qing Prefecture Chang Si had died.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture reported that the former Military Commissioner of Qing Prefecture, Chang Si, had died.

sentences.zh: 己亥，侍衛馬軍都指揮使、夔州節度使樊愛能，侍衛步軍都指揮使、壽州節度使何徽等並諸將校七十餘人，並伏誅。

translations.literal: On day jihai, Cavalry Commander-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Kui Prefecture Fan Aineng, Infantry Commander-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Shou Prefecture He Hui, and more than seventy other generals and officers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day Fan Aineng, Cavalry Commander-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Kui, He Hui, Infantry Commander-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Shou, and more than seventy other generals and officers were all executed.

sentences.zh: 高平之役，兩軍既成列，賊騎來挑戰，愛能望風而退，何徽以徒兵陣於後，為奔騎所突，即時潰亂，二將南走。

translations.literal: At the battle of Gaoping, once the two armies had formed their lines, rebel cavalry came to challenge; Fan Aineng fled at sight of the wind; He Hui had foot soldiers arrayed in the rear, and they were struck by fleeing cavalry and immediately collapsed in disorder; the two generals fled south.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoping, once the armies were drawn up, rebel cavalry came to challenge. Fan Aineng fled at the first sign of trouble. He Hui's infantry in the rear was overrun by fleeing horsemen and broke at once. Both generals fled south.

sentences.zh: 帝遣近臣宣諭止遏，莫肯從命，皆揚言曰：「官軍大敗，餘眾已解甲矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent close attendants to proclaim orders to halt them, but none would obey; all shouted aloud: "The government army has suffered a great defeat; the remaining troops have already cast off their armor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent close attendants to order them to stop, but they would not obey. All shouted, "The imperial army is routed—the rest have already thrown down their arms."

sentences.zh: 」至暮，以官軍克捷，方稍稍而回。

translations.literal: " Only at dusk, when the government army had won victory, did they gradually return.
translations.idiomatic: " Only at dusk, when the imperial army had won, did they slowly straggle back.

sentences.zh: 帝至潞州，錄其奔遁者，自軍使以上及監押使臣並斬之，由是驕將墮兵，無不知懼。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Lu Prefecture, he recorded those who had fled; from army commanders upward and supervisory commissioners, all were beheaded; from this arrogant generals and lax soldiers all knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: At Lu Prefecture he recorded every fugitive from army commanders and supervisory commissioners upward and had them beheaded. After that no arrogant general or lax soldier failed to fear the consequences.

sentences.zh: 帝以何徽有平陽守禦之功，欲貸其罪，竟不可，與愛能俱殺之，皆給槥車歸葬。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because He Hui had merit in defending and holding Pingyang, wished to remit his crime, but in the end could not; together with Fan Aineng he was killed, and both were given coffin carts to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Because He Hui had merit in defending Pingyang, the emperor wished to spare him, but in the end could not. He was executed together with Fan Aineng, and both were given coffin carts for burial at home.

translations.literal: (Editorial note:
translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《東都事略》：世宗謂張永德曰：「樊愛能及偏裨七十餘人，吾欲盡按軍法，何如？

translations.literal: (From the 《Outline of the Eastern Capital》: Shizong said to Zhang Yongde: "Fan Aineng and more than seventy junior officers—I wish to punish them all according to military law. What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Outline of the Eastern Capital》: Shizong said to Zhang Yongde, "Fan Aineng and more than seventy junior officers—I want to punish them all under military law. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「必欲開拓疆宇，威加四海，安可已也！

translations.literal: " He replied: "If you must expand territory and spread authority across the four seas, how can this be stopped!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yongde replied, "If you mean to expand the realm and impose your authority on all under heaven, how can you hold back now!"

sentences.zh: 」世宗善其言，悉誅愛能等以徇，軍聲始振。）〉

translations.literal: " Shizong approved his words, executed Fan Aineng and the rest to display as warning, and army morale first revived.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong approved and had Fan Aineng and the rest executed as a public example. Only then did army discipline begin to recover.)]

sentences.zh: 庚子，以侍衛馬步都虞候李重進為許州節度使，以宣徽南院使向訓為滑州節度使，以殿前都指揮使張永德為武信軍節度使，職並如故。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry Deputy Commander Li Chongjin was made Military Commissioner of Xu Prefecture; Southern Court Palace Commissioner Xiang Xun was made Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture; Front Palace Commander-in-Chief Zhang Yongde was made Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army; their duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day Li Chongjin, Deputy Commander of the Palace Guard cavalry and infantry, was made Military Commissioner of Xu; Xiang Xun, Southern Court Palace Commissioner, Military Commissioner of Hua; Zhang Yongde, Front Palace Commander-in-Chief, Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army—all retaining their previous duties.

sentences.zh: 以滑州節度使白重贊為鄜州節度使，以鄭州防禦使史彥超為華州節度使，賞高平之功也。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Bai Chongzan was made Military Commissioner of Bin Prefecture; Defender of Zheng Prefecture Shi Yanchao was made Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture—reward for merit at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chongzan, Military Commissioner of Hua, was transferred to Bin; Shi Yanchao, Defender of Zheng, to Hua—as rewards for the victory at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 以晉州節度使藥元福為同州節度使，以宣徽北院使楊廷璋為晉州節度使，以同州節度使張鐸為彰義軍節度使，以客省使吳延祚為宣徽北院使，以龍捷左廂都指揮使李千為蔡州防禦使，以龍捷右廂都指揮使田中為密州防禦使，以虎捷右廂都指揮使張順為登州防禦使，以龍捷左第二軍都指揮使孫延進為鄭州防禦使，以前耀州團練使符彥能為澤州防禦使，以散員都指揮使李繼勛為殿前都虞候，以殿前都虞候韓令坤為龍捷左廂都指揮使，以鐵騎第一軍都指揮使趙宏殷為龍捷右廂都指揮使，以散員都指揮使慕容延釗為虎捷左廂都指揮使，以控鶴第一軍都指揮使趙鼎為虎捷右廂都指揮使，並遙授團練使，其餘改轉有差。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Jin Prefecture Yao Yuanfu was made Military Commissioner of Tong Prefecture; Northern Court Palace Commissioner Yang Tingzhang was made Military Commissioner of Jin Prefecture; Military Commissioner of Tong Prefecture Zhang Duo was made Military Commissioner of the Zhangyi Army; Reception Commissioner Wu Yanzuo was made Northern Court Palace Commissioner; Dragon Rapid Left Wing Commander-in-Chief Li Qian was made Defender of Cai Prefecture; Dragon Rapid Right Wing Commander-in-Chief Tian Zhong was made Defender of Mi Prefecture; Tiger Rapid Right Wing Commander-in-Chief Zhang Shun was made Defender of Deng Prefecture; Dragon Rapid Left Second Army Commander-in-Chief Sun Yanjin was made Defender of Zheng Prefecture; former Regimental Training Commissioner of Yao Prefecture Fu Yanneng was made Defender of Ze Prefecture; Straggler Commander-in-Chief Li Jixun was made Front Palace Deputy Commander; Front Palace Deputy Commander Han Lingkun was made Dragon Rapid Left Wing Commander-in-Chief; Iron Cavalry First Army Commander-in-Chief Zhao Hongyin was made Dragon Rapid Right Wing Commander-in-Chief; Straggler Commander-in-Chief Murong Yanzhao was made Tiger Rapid Left Wing Commander-in-Chief; Crane Control First Army Commander-in-Chief Zhao Ding was made Tiger Rapid Right Wing Commander-in-Chief; all were remotely granted regimental training commissioner rank; the rest received transfers in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanfu went from Jin to Tong; Yang Tingzhang from Northern Court Palace Commissioner to Jin; Zhang Duo from Tong to the Zhangyi Army; Wu Yanzuo became Northern Court Palace Commissioner. Li Qian, Tian Zhong, Zhang Shun, Sun Yanjin, and Fu Yanneng received prefectural defender posts. Li Jixun became Front Palace Deputy Commander; Han Lingkun, Dragon Rapid Left Wing Commander; Zhao Hongyin, Dragon Rapid Right Wing; Murong Yanzhao, Tiger Rapid Left Wing; Zhao Ding, Tiger Rapid Right Wing. All received remote regimental training commissioner ranks; others were promoted or transferred in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以天雄軍節度使、衛王符彥卿為河東行營都部署，知太原行府事；

translations.literal: On day renyin, Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei Fu Yanqing was made Grand Commander of the Hedong field headquarters and charged with affairs of the Taiyuan field administration;
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day Fu Yanqing, Military Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army and Prince of Wei, was made Grand Commander of the Hedong field headquarters and put in charge of the Taiyuan field administration;

sentences.zh: 以澶州節度使郭崇為行營副部署；

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Cao Prefecture Guo Chong was made Deputy Grand Commander of the field headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chong, Military Commissioner of Cao, was made Deputy Grand Commander of the field headquarters;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使向訓為行營兵馬都監；

translations.literal: Southern Court Palace Commissioner Xiang Xun was made Grand Supervisor of field headquarters troops and horses;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, Southern Court Palace Commissioner, was made Grand Supervisor of field headquarters troops and horses;

sentences.zh: 以侍衛都虞候李重進為行營都虞候。

translations.literal: Palace Guard Deputy Commander Li Chongjin was made Deputy Commander of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, Palace Guard Deputy Commander, was made Deputy Commander of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以華州節度使史彥超為先鋒都指揮使，領步騎二萬，進討河東。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Shi Yanchao was made Vanguard Commander-in-Chief, leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to advance and attack Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanchao, Military Commissioner of Hua, was made Vanguard Commander-in-Chief and led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry against Hedong.

sentences.zh: 詔河中節度使王彥超、陜府節度使韓通，率兵自陰地關討賊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Military Commissioner of Hezhong Wang Yanchao and Military Commissioner of the Shaanfu region Han Tong to lead troops through Yindi Pass to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Yanchao of Hezhong and Han Tong of Shaanfu to lead troops through Yindi Pass against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以河陽節度使劉詞為隨駕都部署，以鄜州節度使白重贊為隨駕副部署。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Heyang Liu Ci was made Grand Commander accompanying the imperial carriage; Military Commissioner of Bin Prefecture Bai Chongzan was made Deputy Grand Commander accompanying the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci, Military Commissioner of Heyang, was made Grand Commander accompanying the emperor; Bai Chongzan, Military Commissioner of Bin, Deputy Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙巳，太祖靈駕發東京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day yisi, Emperor Taizu's catafalque departed the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the yisi day, Emperor Taizu's catafalque departed the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，葬於嵩陵。

translations.literal: On day yimao, he was buried at Songling.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day he was buried at Songling.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王彥超奏，偽汾州防禦使董希顏以城歸順。

sentences.zh: 丁巳，幸柏谷寺。

translations.literal: On day dingsi, the Emperor visited Baigu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day the emperor visited Baigu Temple.

translations.literal: An edict ordered the generals beneath the walls of Hedong to win over the population, forbid plunder, levy only that year's rent and taxes, and grant official status to civilians who contributed five hundred hu of grain or five hundred bundles of fodder, and appoint them to prefectural or county office if they contributed one thousand hu or one thousand bundles.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the generals at Hedong to win over the people, forbid looting, levy only that year's rent and taxes, grant official status to anyone who contributed five hundred hu of grain or five hundred bundles of fodder, and appoint contributors of one thousand hu or one thousand bundles to prefectural or county office.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，符彥卿奏，嵐、憲二州歸順。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Fu Yanqing memorialized that Lan and Xian Prefectures had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Fu Yanqing reported that Lan and Xian Prefectures had submitted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，制立衛國夫人符氏為皇后，仍令有司擇日備禮冊命。

translations.literal: On day renxu, an edict established Lady Fu, Duchess of Weiguo, as empress, and ordered the relevant offices to choose a day and prepare the full investiture ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day an edict established Lady Fu, Duchess of Weiguo, as empress and ordered the relevant offices to choose a day and prepare the full investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 王彥超奏，收下石州，獲偽刺史安彥進。

translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao reported that Shizhou had been taken and the rebel Prefect An Yanjin captured.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，偽沁州刺史李廷誨以城歸順。

translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day Li Tinghui, rebel Prefect of Qin Prefecture, surrendered the city and submitted.

sentences.zh: 甲子，皇妹壽安公主張氏進封晉國長公主。

translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day the emperor's younger sister, Princess Shou'an of the Zhang clan, was advanced in rank to Grand Princess of Jin.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，東京奏，太師、中書令馮道薨。

translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day the Eastern Capital reported that Grand Preceptor and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Feng Dao had died.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，太祖皇帝神主祔於太廟。

translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day the spirit tablet of Emperor Taizu was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 庚午，曲赦潞州見禁罪人，除死罪外並釋放。

translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day a partial amnesty was granted for prisoners held in Lu Prefecture; all except those sentenced to death were released.

sentences.zh: 是日，車駕發潞州，親征劉崇。

translations.literal: That day the imperial carriage departed Lu Prefecture on a personal campaign against Liu Chong.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor departed Lu Prefecture on a personal campaign against Liu Chong.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，忻州偽監軍李殺刺史趙臯及契丹大將楊耨姑，以州城歸順。

translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Li, rebel military supervisor of Xin Prefecture, killed Prefect Zhao Gao and the Khitan Grand General Yang Nougu and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 詔授李忻州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li as Military Commissioner of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li was appointed Military Commissioner of Xin by edict.

translations.idiomatic: That day Zheng Chuqian, rebel Defender of Dai Prefecture, surrendered the city and submitted.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，觀兵於太原城下，帝親自慰勉，錫賚有差。

translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day troops were reviewed beneath the walls of Taiyuan; the emperor personally consoled and encouraged them, and rewards were granted in varying degrees.

translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day An Yanjin, rebel-appointed Prefect of Shizhou, was beheaded beneath the walls of Taiyuan for resisting the imperial army.

translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day Guo Congyi, former Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army, was made Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army.

translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day Fu Prefecture was elevated to a military commission under the name Yong'an Army, and Zhe Deyi, Defender of the prefecture, was made Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯朔，詔班師，車駕發離太原。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, day guimao, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army; the imperial carriage departed Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, the guimao day, an edict ordered withdrawal; the emperor departed Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時大集兵賦，及征山東、懷、孟、蒲、陜丁夫數萬，急攻其城，旦夕之間，期於必取。

translations.idiomatic: At that time troops and levies had been massed in great numbers, and tens of thousands of laborers from east of the mountains and from Huai, Meng, Pu, and Shaan had been conscripted for an urgent assault expected to take the city within days.

sentences.zh: 會大雨時行，軍士勞苦，復以忻口之師不振，帝遂決旋師之意。

translations.literal: Then heavy rain fell in season; the soldiers were worn with labor; moreover the force at Xinkou had not prospered; the Emperor thereupon decided on withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Then seasonal heavy rains fell, the soldiers were exhausted, and the force at Xinkou had faltered; the emperor thereupon decided to withdraw.

translations.idiomatic: Li Jun of Lu was additionally appointed Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 河中王彥超移鎮許州，加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was transferred to Xu Prefecture and additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao of Hezhong was moved to Xu and additionally appointed Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 許州節度、侍衛都虞候李重進移鎮宋州，加同平章事兼侍衛親軍都指揮使；

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Xu Prefecture and Palace Guard Deputy Commander Li Chongjin was transferred to Song Prefecture, additionally made Associate Grand Councilor and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Personal Army;
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, Military Commissioner of Xu and Palace Guard Deputy Commander, was transferred to Song Prefecture, additionally made Associate Grand Councilor and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Personal Army;

sentences.zh: 以武信軍節度使兼殿前都指揮使張永德為滑州節度使，加檢校太傅，典軍如故；

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army and concurrent Front Palace Commander-in-Chief Zhang Yongde was made Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture, additionally made Honorary Grand Tutor, and continued to command the army as before;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, Military Commissioner of the Wuxin Army and Front Palace Commander-in-Chief, was made Military Commissioner of Hua, additionally Honorary Grand Tutor, and continued to command the army as before;

sentences.zh: 同州藥元福移鎮陜州，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu of Tong Prefecture was transferred to Shaan Prefecture and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanfu of Tong was transferred to Shaan and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 鄜州白重贊移鎮河陽，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: Bai Chongzan of Bin Prefecture was transferred to Heyang and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Chongzan of Bin was transferred to Heyang and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 陜州韓通移鎮曹州，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Han Tong of Shaan Prefecture was transferred to Cao Prefecture and additionally made Honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong of Shaan was transferred to Cao and additionally made Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝即位之初，覃慶於諸侯，是賞從征之功也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Emperor's accession, broad celebrations were extended to the feudatories—this was reward for merit in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the emperor's reign, broad honors were extended to the feudatories—reward for merit in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以前禮部侍郎邊光範為刑部侍郎，權判開封府事。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, former Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Bian Guangfan was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and provisionally assigned to administer Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day Bian Guangfan, former Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and provisionally assigned to administer Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，天下兵馬元帥、吳越國王錢俶加天下兵馬都元帥；

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven and King of Wuyue Qian Chu was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day Qian Chu, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven and King of Wuyue, was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 襄州節度使、陳王安審琦加守太尉。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Xiang Prefecture and Prince of Chen An Shenqi was additionally made Guardian Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi, Military Commissioner of Xiang and Prince of Chen, was additionally made Guardian Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，右散騎常侍張可復卒。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Zhang Kefu died.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day Zhang Kefu, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, died.

sentences.zh: 以前亳州防禦使李萬金為鄜州留後。

translations.literal: Former Defender of Bo Prefecture Li Wanjin was made Acting Commander of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanjin, former Defender of Bo Prefecture, was made Acting Commander of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，幸南莊。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, the Emperor visited Nanzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day the emperor visited Nanzhuang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，荊南節度使、南平王高保融加守中書令，夏州節度使、西平王李彜興加守太保，西京留守武行德、徐州王晏、鄧州侯章並加兼中書令。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping Gao Baorong was additionally made Guardian Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture and Prince of Xiping Li Yixing was additionally made Guardian Grand Guardian; Military Governor of the Western Capital Wu Xingde, Wang Yan of Xu Prefecture, and Hou Zhang of Deng Prefecture were all additionally made Directors of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Gao Baorong, Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Prince of Nanping, was additionally made Guardian Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Li Yixing, Military Commissioner of Xia and Prince of Xiping, Guardian Grand Guardian; Wu Xingde, Military Governor of the Western Capital, Wang Yan of Xu, and Hou Zhang of Deng were all additionally made Directors of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 癸未，湖南王進逵加兼中書令；

translations.literal: On day guimao, Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day Wang Jinkui of Hunan was additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 天德軍節度使郭勛、邠州折從阮、安州李洪義並加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army Guo Xun, Zhe Congruan of Bin Prefecture, and Li Hongyi of An Prefecture were all additionally made Palace Attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun, Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army, Zhe Congruan of Bin, and Li Hongyi of An were all additionally made Palace Attendants;

sentences.zh: 以前華州節度使孫方諫為同州節度使，加兼中書令；

translations.literal: Former Military Commissioner of Hua Prefecture Sun Fangjian was made Military Commissioner of Tong Prefecture and additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat concurrently;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fangjian, former Military Commissioner of Hua, was made Military Commissioner of Tong and additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat concurrently;

sentences.zh: 以前永興軍節度使王仁鎬為河中節度使，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Former Military Commissioner of the Yongxing Army Wang Renhao was made Military Commissioner of Hezhong and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renhao, former Military Commissioner of the Yongxing Army, was made Military Commissioner of Hezhong and additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，滄州李暉、貝州王饒、鎮州曹英並加兼侍中，涇州張鐸、相州王進、延州袁鳷並加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Li Hui of Cang Prefecture, Wang Rao of Bei Prefecture, and Cao Ying of Zhen Prefecture were all additionally made Palace Attendants concurrently; Zhang Duo of Jing Prefecture, Wang Jin of Xiang Prefecture, and Yuan Zhi of Yan Prefecture were all additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day Li Hui of Cang, Wang Rao of Bei, and Cao Ying of Zhen were all additionally made Palace Attendants concurrently; Zhang Duo of Jing, Wang Jin of Xiang, and Yuan Zhi of Yan were all additionally made Honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，百僚上表，請以九月二十四日誕聖日為天清節，從之。

translations.literal: On day renchen, the hundred officials submitted a memorial requesting that the birth day on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month be established as the Tianqing Festival; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day the hundred officials submitted a memorial requesting that the emperor's birthday, the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, be established as the Tianqing Festival. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以左僕射兼門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史範質為守司徒兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士；

translations.literal: On day guisi, Left Vice Director Fan Zhi, concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History, was made Guardian Grand Tutor concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall;
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day Fan Zhi, Left Vice Director concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History, was made Guardian Grand Tutor concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall;

translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《國老談苑》云：周太祖嘗令世宗詣範質，時為親王，軒車高大，門不能容，世宗即下馬步入。

translations.literal: (The 《Guolao tanyuan》 states: Zhou Taizu once had Shizong call on Fan Zhi; at the time he was a prince. His carriage was tall and the gate could not accommodate it, so Shizong at once dismounted and entered on foot.

sentences.zh: 以左僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士、判三司李穀為守司徒兼門下侍朗、平章事，監修國史；

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Li Gu, concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, and Administrator of the Three Offices, was made Guardian Grand Tutor concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History;
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, Left Vice Director concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, and Administrator of the Three Offices, was made Guardian Grand Tutor concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History;

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事王溥為中書侍郎兼禮部尚書、平章事、集賢殿大學士；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Pu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrently Minister of Rites, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrently Minister of Rites, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall;

sentences.zh: 以樞密院學士、工部侍郎景範為中書侍郎、平章事，判三司；

translations.literal: Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works Jing Fan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Administrator of the Three Offices;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fan, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Administrator of the Three Offices;

sentences.zh: 樞密使、檢校太保、同平章事鄭仁誨加兼侍中；

translations.literal: Commissioner of Military Affairs, Honorary Grand Guardian, and Associate Director of the Imperial Secretariat Zheng Renhui was additionally made Palace Attendant concurrently;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Renhui, Commissioner of Military Affairs, Honorary Grand Guardian, and Associate Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was additionally made Palace Attendant concurrently;

sentences.zh: 靈武馮繼業、定州孫行友、邢州田景鹹並加檢校太傅；

translations.literal: Feng Jiye of Lingwu, Sun Xingyou of Ding Prefecture, and Tian Jingxian of Xing Prefecture were all additionally made Honorary Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jiye of Lingwu, Sun Xingyou of Ding, and Tian Jingxian of Xing were all additionally made Honorary Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 晉州楊廷璋加檢校太保；

translations.literal: Yang Tingzhang of Jin Prefecture was additionally made Honorary Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tingzhang of Jin was additionally made Honorary Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事趙上交為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Zhao Shangjiao was made Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao, Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, was made Guest of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以樞密副使、右監門衛大將軍魏仁浦為樞密使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: On day yiwei, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and Major General of the Right Gate Guard Command Wei Renpu was made Commissioner of Military Affairs and Honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day Wei Renpu, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and Major General of the Right Gate Guard Command, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs and Honorary Grand Guardian.

translations.idiomatic: [Note:

sentences.zh: （《東都事略》云：議者以仁浦不由科第進，世宗曰：「顧才何如耳！

translations.literal: (From the 《Outline of the Eastern Capital》: Critics objected that Renpu had not advanced through the civil service examinations. Shizong said: "Talent is what matters!
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Outline of the Eastern Capital》: Critics objected that Renpu had not risen through the civil service examinations. Shizong said, "What matters is talent!
